```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2) 
library(readxl) 
library(lubridate)
library(janitor) 
library(viridis) 
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest) 
library(broom) 
library(equatiomatic)


# Global options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

study_dat <- read.csv("../CleanData/study_dat.csv") 

study_dat <- study_dat |> 
  mutate(year = as.factor(year),
         date_sampled = ymd(date_sampled), 
         log_conc = log(silica_conc))
```

# Introduction 

The following data exploration will produce descriptive statistics and explore the distribution of data in terms of duration of exposure for use of an AIHA abstract. 


# General Data Summaries   

How many observations? 
```{r}
nrow(study_dat)
``` 

How many are detect vs. non-detect? 

```{r}
study_dat |> 
count(loq) |> 
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)

```

## Study Period 

I.E., what dates/years are covered by the time series data? 

```{r}
range(study_dat$date_sampled)
```

### Detected Data 


```{r} 
study_dat |> 
  filter(loq == FALSE) |> 
  summarize(min(date_sampled), max(date_sampled)) 

``` 

Among our *detected* measurements, we have samples ranging from 11/14/2006 to 12/30/2025.  

What month had the most detects? 

```{r}
study_dat |> 
  filter(loq == FALSE) |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  count() |> 
  arrange(desc(n))
```

### Non-Detects 

```{r}
study_dat |> 
  filter(loq == TRUE) |> 
  summarize(min(date_sampled), max(date_sampled))
```

Among our *non-detect* samples, we have samples ranging from 2/23/2004 to 3/05/2025.   



# Subsetting datasets 

We are now going to make some new datasets, one which contains just our non-detect measurements, one with our detected measurements, and one that has both. 

```{r}
all_data <- study_dat  
nrow(all_data)

non_detects <- study_dat |> 
  filter(loq == TRUE) 
nrow(non_detects)

study_dat <- study_dat |> 
  filter(loq == FALSE) 
nrow(study_dat)

```
  
# Non-Detect examination  

Min and max number per year: 

```{r}
non_detects |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  summarize(n = n()) |> 
  arrange(desc(n))
```

How many non-detects relative to detects per year?

```{r}
all_data |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
count(loq) |> 
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)
```
  
  Plotting this: 
  
```{r}
  loq_summary <- all_data |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  count(loq) |> 
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |> 
  ungroup()


ggplot(loq_summary, aes(x = factor(year), y = pct, fill = loq)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct), "%")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Percent of samples", fill = "Non-Detect Sample")
```
Just eyeballing this, it looks like there could be a significant trend in decreased percent of non-detect samples relative to all samples taken year by year. That could be an interesting model option to investigate further down in the temporal trend section.

## Duration

### Concentration by Duration 

```{r}
study_dat |> 
  group_by(duration) |>
``` 

# Plots 

## AL and PEL plot 

```{r}
# --- Prep: order duration groups, label lod status ---
plot_dat <- study_dat %>%
  mutate(
    duration = factor(duration,
                         levels = c("Task-Based", "Short-Term", "Medium-Term", "Long-Term")),
    lod_status = factor(lod, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
                         labels = c("Reported Measurement", "Below LOD"))
  ) 

al_pel_plot <- ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = duration, y = silica_conc, shape = lod_status, color = lod_status)) +
  
  # Reported Measurement: drawn first (bottom layer), semi-transparent
  geom_jitter(
    data = subset(plot_dat, lod_status == "Reported Measurement"),
    width = 0.15, size = 1.3, alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  
  # Below LOD: drawn second (top layer), fully opaque, no alpha
  geom_jitter(
    data = subset(plot_dat, lod_status == "Below LOD"),
    width = 0.15, size = 1.3, alpha = 1
  ) +

  # Reference limits (fixed colors via override so they don't clash with the point color scale)
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 25, linetype = "Action Level (25 µg/m³)"),
             color = "#ff7f0e", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 50, linetype = "PEL (50 µg/m³)"),
             color = "#d62728", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 5000), 
    limits = c(1, 6000)
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Measurement Type",
    values = c("Reported Measurement" = 16,
               "Below LOD" = 17)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Measurement Type",
    values = c("Reported Measurement" = "grey40",
               "Below LOD" = "black")
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    name = "Reference Limits",
    values = c("Action Level (25 µg/m³)" = "dashed",
               "PEL (50 µg/m³)" = "dotdash")
  ) +
  guides(
    linetype = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = c("#ff7f0e", "#d62728")))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "RCS Concentration (µg/m³) [Log10 Scale]"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical", 
    legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"),
     legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9)
  ) 

print(al_pel_plot)

ggsave("../Output/duration_concentration_plot.png", al_pel_plot)
```

# Temporal Trends  

## LOQ trends over time  

I'm interested to see if the percentage of non-detects relative to all samples taken changed significantly over the study period. Let's fit a logistic regression.

```{r} 

all_data %>% 
  filter(is.na(establishment)) %>% 
  nrow()

loq_mod_dat <- all_data |>
  mutate(year   = as.numeric(as.character(year)),
         nd     = as.integer(loq),        # 1 = non-detect
         year_c = year - min(year)) 

loq_glm <- glm(nd ~ year_c, family = binomial, data = loq_mod_dat)
summary(loq_glm)
exp(cbind(OR = coef(loq_glm), confint(loq_glm)))


#cluster-robust: 

vc_cl <- vcovCL(loq_glm, cluster = ~ establishment, type = "HC1") 

coeftest(loq_glm, vcov. = vc_cl) 
exp(coef(loq_glm, vcov. = vc_cl))
exp(coefci(loq_glm, vcov. = vc_cl))   


#R^2 value 

library(performance)

r2_mcfadden(loq_glm)

r2_mcfadden(loq_glm, vcov. = vc_cl)


```  
Let's repeat, this time ignoring the year 2004: 
```{r}


loq_mod_dat2 <- all_data |>
  filter(year != "2004") %>% 
  mutate(year   = as.numeric(as.character(year)),
         nd     = as.integer(loq)) 

loq_glm2 <- glm(nd ~ year, family = binomial, data = loq_mod_dat2)
summary(loq_glm2)
exp(cbind(OR = coef(loq_glm2), confint(loq_glm2)))


#cluster-robust: 

vc_cl <- vcovCL(loq_glm2, cluster = ~ establishment, type = "HC1") 

coeftest(loq_glm2, vcov. = vc_cl) 
exp(coef(loq_glm2, vcov. = vc_cl))
exp(coefci(loq_glm2, vcov. = vc_cl))    

r2_mcfadden(loq_glm2)

```



Investigating a mixed model (although we ultimately will not report on it):
```{r}
#how many establishments have repeated measurements? How many per year?
all_data |>
     group_by(establishment) |>
     summarise(n_years = n_distinct(year)) |>
     count(n_years)


#mixed-effects 
library(lme4)
loq_glmm <- glmer(nd ~ year_c + (1 | establishment),
                  family = binomial, data = loq_mod_dat)
summary(loq_glmm)
exp(fixef(loq_glmm)) 


```

## Median concentration reported per year 

The OSHA citations database was used to analyze the median concentration reported per year. We can replicate the same analysis:  

Do we have all of the years covered by this data? 

```{r}

study_dat |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  count()


``` 

We're good!

###Checks for normality 

```{r}
qqnorm(study_dat$silica_conc) 
hist(study_dat$silica_conc)
shapiro.test(study_dat$silica_conc)
```

Let's log-transform and check again: 

```{r}
study_dat <- study_dat |> 
  mutate(log_conc = log(silica_conc)) 


hist(study_dat$log_conc)
shapiro.test(study_dat$log_conc)

```


## Crude mod:  

Get the median by year first, then fit linear trend. 

Issue: we can't easily log-transform data with so many zeros.  

How many zeroes were censored?? 

```{r}
study_dat |> 
  filter(silica_conc == 0) |> 
  count() 

study_dat |> 
  filter(silica_conc == 0) |>  
  group_by(imis) |> 
  count()
 
no_zeros_dat <- study_dat|> 
  filter(silica_conc != 0) 


```

```{r}
mod_median_trend <- lm(log_conc ~ as.numeric(year), data = no_zeros_dat) 

summary(mod_median_trend) 

exp(coef(mod_median_trend))  

ci_log <- cbind(estimate = coef(mod_median_trend), confint(mod_median_trend))
ci_ratio <- exp(ci_log)
ci_ratio

round((ci_ratio[2, ] - 1) * 100, 1)  

#cluster-robust:

coeftest(mod_median_trend,
         vcov = vcovCL(mod_median_trend,
                       cluster = ~ establishment,
                       type = "HC1"))  

cluster <- coeftest(mod_median_trend,
         vcov = vcovCL(mod_median_trend,
                       cluster = ~ establishment,
                       type = "HC1"))  


ci_log_cluster <- cbind(estimate = coef(cluster), confint(cluster))
ci_ratio_cluster <- exp(ci_log_cluster)
ci_ratio_cluster

round((ci_ratio_cluster[2, ] - 1) * 100, 1) 

```
There is a statistically significant relationship here whereby the median concentration increases by 1.3 units for each additional year in the study period.  


## Median by Duration 

Get the median by year and duration:

```{r}
median_by_year_and_duration <- no_zeros_dat|> 
  group_by(year,duration) |>
  mutate(log_conc = log(silica_conc))


mod_median_trend2 <- lm(log_conc ~ as.numeric(year)*duration, data = median_by_year_and_duration)
summary(mod_median_trend2)
```


There is no significant trend when we differentiate by duration.


# All measurements 

### Over PEL

What if we instead investigate a logistic model that investigates whether the number of facilities exceeding the PEL has changed over the years? 

```{r} 



mod_logistic  <- glm(over_PEL~as.numeric(year), data = no_zeros_dat, 
                     family = binomial)
summary(mod_logistic) 
extract_eq(mod_logistic)
``` 

No significant relationship here. 

We should not need to control for establishment here, since we are only looking at whether the proportion of facilities over PEL changed by year, but we can add in a random effect for establishment either way: 

```{r}

coeftest(mod_logistic,
         vcov = vcovCL(mod_logistic,
                       cluster = ~ establishment,
                       type = "HC1")) 
```  



# Do Establishments improve over time? 

We want to check out the establishments that have multiple observations, and investigate whether they improve over time: 


Some establishments have multiple samples on the same day, so we will take the median conc only for those instances: 

```{r}
est_daily <- study_dat |> 
  group_by(establishment, date_sampled) |> 
  summarize(median_conc = median(silica_conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
``` 

Next we only keep establishments with multiple distinct sampling dates: 

```{r}
est_multi <- est_daily |> 
  group_by(establishment) |> #just looking at establishment
  filter(n() >= 2) |> #only those that have multiple measurements
  arrange(establishment, date_sampled)#in order of date sampled
``` 


Let's figure out the change between consecutive measurements: 

```{r}
est_changes <- est_multi |> 
  group_by(establishment) |> 
  mutate(
    conc_change = median_conc - lag(median_conc), #median conc measurement MINUS the previous one
    days_elapsed = as.numeric(date_sampled - lag(date_sampled)), #number of days between consecuitve measurements
    years_elapsed = days_elapsed / 365.25, #converting days into years
    rate_per_year = conc_change / years_elapsed #the change in establishments divided by time elaspsed
  ) |> 
  filter(!is.na(conc_change))  #removing rows where conc_change is NA (each establishment's first row -- only retaining a measured change between two timepoints)
```

```{r}
est_changes

est_changes |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(rate_per_year, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rate = median(rate_per_year, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#NOTE: this includes changes between the same establishment at different time points (i.e., if an establishment was measured 3 times, it will contribute 2 changes below)
est_changes |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(direction = case_when(
    conc_change < 0 ~ "improved",
    conc_change > 0 ~ "worsened",
    TRUE ~ "unchanged"
  )) |> 
  count(direction) |> 
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n))
```


```{r, fig.height=20, fig.width=20} 
ggplot(est_multi, aes(x = date_sampled, y = median_conc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ establishment, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Date sampled", y = "Median silica concentration") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7))

```
